Label says add water in two portions, shake between. Added the first portion, drive-thru bell went, came back and added two more because I thought I hadn't started yet. Went to cap it and the liquid was clearly over the fill line. Dumped it, remade it. Would have been roughly two-thirds strength for a 10 day course. If it had landed under the line I don't think I'd have known.

records.text: Two art sticks back to back, beds 4 and 6 in SICU, both vented, both on the list to have gases back before the team started rounds. Drew 4, went straight to 6, carried both syringes on ice to the analyzer and put the labels on there. They got swapped. Bed 6 showed a PaCO2 of 61 - that was bed 4's - so the resident bumped 6's rate from 14 to 20. Repeat on 6 an hour later: pH 7.57, CO2 24. Bed 4 sat hypercapnic with nothing changed. Figured out when the two sets of numbers made no sense together. Both back on prior settings. Doing them together saves a trip, is the honest answer.

records.text: Cross-cover, 0130. Paged for BP 196/108, pt with hx HTN, no symptoms. Typed 'hydr' into order search and clicked what I thought was hydralazine 10 mg IV. It was hydroxyzine 25 mg PO, which sorts first, and in that dropdown both names get cut off to 'HYDR...ZINE' unless you hover. Recheck at 0230 still 190s and pt very drowsy, RN called me back, that's when we saw it. Gave hydralazine, BP came down. Sleepy till morning, otherwise fine. I'd been up since 0700 the day before, for what that's worth.

records.text: AM draws, 4th floor. Rm 409 was a hard stick, got her on the second try in the L forearm. While I was labeling at the bedside her roommate started calling out for help to the bathroom so I got him up and walked him over. Came back, grabbed the tubes and my tray and moved on to 410. Tourniquet was still on 409's arm. RN found it at ~0730 under the gown sleeve. Hand swollen and mottled, pulses present, improved once it was off, no lasting injury per the team so far. That was the last room of 22 on my run. Taking it off is the one thing I never forget, and I did.

records.text: Floated from ortho to CSU at 1500. Mandatory, my 4th 12 this week. Assigned 5, one of them post-cath with a R femoral sheath due out at 1800. I've never pulled a sheath. Told charge. Oozing at 1930, hematoma by 2000, Hgb down 1.8, vascular came up and placed a compression device. I asked at 1500 not to take the sheath pt. There wasn't anyone else to give it to.

records.text: 0705, rm 11, day +9 allo transplant, 1 unit PRBC, irradiated product required. Night RN had picked the unit up from blood bank before report. I scanned band and bag at the bedside - green check - and spiked it. She was going to come back in and read the tag with me before I started, but 14 was vomiting and she was still trying to finish report on her others. The scan had already come back good, so in my head the matching was done, and I started at 50 mL/h. She came in at 0725 and read the tag: no irradiation sticker. About 15 mL in. Stopped, BB notified, heme aware, workup per protocol, pt afebrile and stable. The scanner matches pt to unit. It doesn't know about special requirements.

classification.label: TECH
classification.reasoning: The bedside scanner returned a "green check" that covered only patient-to-unit matching, and that signal stood in for the tag read that would have caught the missing irradiation sticker — as the reporter puts it, "it doesn't know about special requirements."
